answer: Adding async to a CPU-bound while loop does not prevent a production freeze because the loop still executes synchronously on the CPU, consuming all available CPU time and blocking the event loop. The async keyword only affects I/O operations, not CPU-intensive work. If the loop performs heavy computation, it will continue to occupy the CPU, preventing other tasks—including timers and I/O—from progressing, leading to a perceived freeze. This is a misunderstanding of how async/await works in CPU-bound contexts.

A CPU-bound loop, even if wrapped in `async`, will still consume 100% of the CPU core, causing the process to be unresponsive and effectively freezing the event loop.
